seoTitle: How to Verify Your Identity on Stripe and Go Live
metaDescription: Complete Stripe's identity verification process, upload the right documents, and activate your account to start accepting live payments.
intro: Before you can accept real customer payments, Stripe requires you to complete identity verification and move your account out of test mode. This guide covers the verification process, what documents you'll typically need, and how to activate your account fully.

steps.heading: Start the verification process
steps.body: In your Stripe dashboard, locate the account activation or verification section to begin the process.

steps.heading: Prepare the required documents
steps.body: Gather identification documents appropriate for your account type, whether you're verifying as an individual or a business.

steps.heading: Upload your documents
steps.body: Submit the required documents through Stripe's verification flow, making sure images are clear and unedited.

steps.heading: Avoid common KYC mistakes
steps.body: Double-check that names, addresses, and document details match exactly what's on file to avoid delays in verification.

steps.heading: Move from test to live mode
steps.body: Once verification is approved, switch your account to live mode so you can begin accepting real customer payments.

faq.question: What documents does Stripe require for verification?
faq.answer: Requirements vary by account type and country, but individuals and businesses are generally asked for identification and business registration documents where applicable.

faq.question: How long does Stripe identity verification take?
faq.answer: Verification times vary, but it can range from a few minutes to a few business days depending on your documents and account type.

faq.question: Can I accept payments before verification is complete?
faq.answer: You can typically test your integration in test mode, but real payments require completed verification and an activated account.

faq.question: What happens if my verification is rejected?
faq.answer: Stripe will usually explain the reason for rejection, and you can resubmit corrected or clearer documents to try again.
